findings.description: BER decoder allocates/reads a buffer sized by the attacker-controlled ASN.1 length field without any upper bound, enabling memory exhaustion (resource consumption DoS).
findings.reasoning: IntegerPayloadDecoder.valueDecoder passes the parsed BER `length` directly into readFromStream(substrate, length, options). readFromStream (pyasn1/codec/streaming.py:187) executes `received = substrate.read(size)` with that size, so an attacker controls the number of bytes the decoder attempts to buffer, and the whole chunk is then materialized again via `bytes(chunk)` and `int.from_bytes(...)` doubling memory pressure. There is no maximum-length check or configured cap in the decoder path investigated (no occurrences of a max-length/limit guard found in the decoder module), so a crafted INTEGER/BOOLEAN TLV header with an enormous length value (e.g. 0x04 0x84 0x7fffffff) forces a multi-gigabyte read attempt on non-definite-length substrates / large in-memory substrates. This is a genuine, unbounded-input-size allocation driven by parsed length (CWE-770/CWE-400). Severity is low because typical usage feeds a fully-buffered bytes substrate where the read is bounded by the actual buffer size, and the impact is limited to resource exhaustion, not memory corruption. Two identical CodeQL results were reported at this same line (duplicate).

evidence.code_context: IntegerPayloadDecoder.valueDecoder: `for chunk in readFromStream(substrate, length, options):` then `value = int.from_bytes(bytes(chunk), 'big', signed=True)`. `length` comes from the BER length octets parsed by SingleItemDecoder (stDecodeLength) with no upper-bound validation.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: BER input bytes -> length octets parsed -> `length` parameter of valueDecoder -> readFromStream(substrate, length, ...) -> substrate.read(size) (streaming.py:187) -> buffer of size `length` allocated/read; result duplicated by bytes(chunk) and int.from_bytes.
evidence.notes: grep_search for length-limit guards (max length/maxLength/limit) in pyasn1/codec/ber/decoder.py returned no matches, confirming absence of a cap. Two identical query results pointed at line 145 (duplicate reporting).

findings.description: BER length field is decoded from attacker-controlled input with no upper bound (explicitly acknowledged in a comment), and that unbounded length is later passed to substrate.read()/readFromStream(), enabling memory-exhaustion DoS for streams that materialize the requested size.
findings.reasoning: In `SingleItemDecoder.__call__` (state `stDecodeLength`), the length-of-value is read from the wire: a long-form length of up to 127 length octets is accepted and shifted into `length` with no sanity cap (the source comment literally states "missing check on maximum size"). The resulting `length` is then handed to the payload decoders, which call `readFromStream(substrate, length, options)` -> `substrate.read(size)` (streaming.py:218). For substrate types whose `read(n)` pre-allocates a buffer of `n` bytes (e.g. `io.Buffered*`/file-backed or C-level readers), a crafted header such as `04 88 FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF ...` can demand an enormous allocation before any data is available, producing a memory-exhaustion / DoS condition (CWE-400). Because `readFromStream` also keeps `substrate.seek(-len(received), os.SEEK_CUR)` on short reads, repeated truncated inputs are re-buffered, amplifying the effect. Impact is availability-only and depends on the stream implementation used by the caller, hence marking this as needing manual review rather than a confirmed high-severity TP; pyasn1 upstream considers the practical risk low (the comment shows the maintainers deliberately skipped the check).

evidence.code_context: Length decoding at decoder.py:1650-1682 builds `length` from up to 127 octets with no maximum-value check; consumers include AbstractSimplePayloadDecoder.substrateCollector (decoder.py:71) and AnyPayloadDecoder/OpenType (decoder.py:1323) which do `readFromStream(substrate, length, options)`.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: attacker bytes -> readFromStream(substrate,1) firstOctet -> size = firstOctet & 0x7F -> readFromStream(substrate,size) encodedLength -> length = (length<<8)|octet (unbounded) -> valueDecoder(substrate, ..., length=length) -> readFromStream(substrate, length) -> substrate.read(length) (streaming.py:218).
evidence.notes: streaming.py:218 `received = substrate.read(size)` is the actual allocation site. Code comment at decoder.py:1669-1670 acknowledges: 'missing check on maximum size, which shouldn't be a problem, we can handle more than is possible'. Realistic exploitation requires a substrate whose read() pre-allocates (e.g. BytesIO/readinto-based wrappers) and is otherwise bounded by available input.
